## 1. Bottom line
COIN is in a well-established downtrend. Price, short-term momentum, and the volume-weighted trend all point down. The only counter-signals are a mildly oversold RSI and a possible, unconfirmed RSI divergence. The data does not show a confirmed reversal. The 2026-11-10 close of 132.13 is the lowest close in the 128-row window (2026-05-11 to 2026-11-10).

All exact figures below come from the verified snapshot or from rows of the price data. The tools give no news or fundamental context, so I cannot explain the 2026-10-30 gap-down.

- **Trend:** close_50_sma, close_200_sma, close_10_ema. These cover medium, long, and short horizons.
- **Momentum:** macd and rsi. MACD measures trend momentum and RSI measures overbought/oversold. The snapshot also supplied macds and macdh, which I use for the MACD read.
- **Volatility:** boll_lb and atr. The lower band marks oversold extremes and ATR sizes risk. The snapshot also supplied boll (middle) and boll_ub.
- **Volume:** vwma, to check whether volume supports the price trend.

- **Moving averages:** 10 EMA 143.69, 50 SMA 173.38, 200 SMA 175.18.

- **RSI:** 32.82.

- **Price vs. averages:** price sits below every average. It is about 11.6 points under the 10 EMA (143.69), about 15.6 under the VWMA (147.74), about 41.3 under the 50 SMA (173.38), and about 43.1 under the 200 SMA (175.18).

- **50/200 SMA relationship:** the 50 SMA is below the 200 SMA (173.38 vs. 175.18), a bearish alignment. It is not a fresh cross within the 30-day window. The 50 SMA was already below the 200 SMA on 2026-10-12 (175.25 vs. 183.47). The gap narrowed from about 8.2 to about 1.8 points, mainly because the 200 SMA fell faster. Any further convergence would be a lagging artifact, not bullish evidence, since price is far below both.
- **Lower highs and lower lows since the September peak:**
  - The window's last big push peaked with a 2026-09-21 high of 208.33.
  - Later swing highs were 185.49 (2026-10-15), 180.60 (2026-10-21), and 153.33 (2026-11-04).

- **Breakdown event (2026-10-30):** the stock gapped down (open 148.23 after a 160.59 close) and closed at 143.54 on 20.89M shares. That is among the heaviest-volume sessions in the window, comparable to 20.87M on 2026-07-31. The 2026-11-04 rebound to 151.50 failed the next day (2026-11-05 close 136.82, volume 12.55M).
- **Prior lows now broken:** the 2026-06-26 low (139.18) and the 2026-07-31 low (139.11) were both reached earlier in the window. Price has since traded below them, so those levels are no longer holding.

- **MACD:** the line (-11.53) is below its signal (-9.13) and below zero, with a histogram of -2.40. It crossed from positive (+0.32 on 2026-10-12) to negative and has trended lower since. The pace of decline has slowed. It fell about 1.5 points per day around 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-02, but only about 0.4 to 0.8 per day in the last three sessions. That is deceleration, not a bullish crossover.
- **RSI:** 32.82, just above the 30 oversold threshold. It closed below 30 at 29.70 on 2026-11-02, bounced to 40.65 on 2026-11-04, and rolled back over.

- **Bands:** the lower band is 124.98, only 7.15 points below the close. The middle band is 157.08 and the upper is 189.17. The lower band was about 170 on 2026-10-15 and has collapsed, so volatility has expanded sharply.
- **Band tests:** price closed below the lower band on 2026-10-30 (143.54 vs. 149.81) and 2026-11-02 (137.83 vs. 143.96). It has not closed below the lower band in the three sessions since. The 2026-11-10 low of 129.41 stayed above the 124.98 band.

- **ATR:** 10.39, roughly 7.9% of the close. It ranged between 9.40 (2026-10-29) and 11.14 (2026-10-16) over the window. Daily swings are large. A 1.5 ATR buffer is about 15.6 points and a 2 ATR buffer is about 20.8 points. Tight stops are likely to be hit by noise, and position size should be reduced accordingly.

Conservative Analyst: I'll start with where I agree, because it narrows the disagreement. The trend is down, the tape is bearish, and I'm not arguing for covering everything and flipping long. My objection is to two specific parts of the plan: adding to the short here, and the way it protects the profit we already have.

A reward-to-risk ratio means little without a hit rate, and a stop that tight on a 3.35-beta stock will get hit by ordinary movement far more often than the ratio implies. At a 1.8 to 1 ratio the break-even hit rate is about 36%, and the 3.6 to 1 tranche needs only about 22%, so the add doesn't need to be right most of the time. It does need a stop that isn't noise, and 154 on a close, about 1.5 to 2 ATR from the fills, is defensible.

Last, refresh the COIN news pull before any resting order goes live, and revisit the levels daily since the moving averages keep falling. If the charter approval turns out to be real, skip the add and lean on the trim.

That keeps the Sell and the edge the aggressive analyst wants, answers the conservative analyst's concern about the $200 of open profit, and avoids both selling the low in full and sitting on an unprotected position.
